strategy_title: Enlarging Tiles Increases Smem Pressure, Halves Occupancy
strategy_description: Replacing the tl.trans(b_T) B-load pattern with a canonical [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] direct load while simultaneously doubling BLOCK_M (32→64) and BLOCK_K (32→64) caused an 82% regression (0.55x speedup). Despite the bank conflict count remaining similarly high (SharedMemoryConflicts wavefronts ~745k→799k, bank-conflict way average worsened from 12 to 18), the dominant effect was that the larger tile sizes tripled dynamic shared memory per block (16→49 KB), cutting the shared-memory-limited block count from 9 to 4 per SM and halving theoretical occupancy from 50% to 25%. Registers per thread also jumped from 64 to 92, further constraining occupancy. The net result was a 83% increase in kernel duration (47.94→87.58 µs) with achieved occupancy unchanged at 6.25% — the GPU remained equally underutilized but each tile now took longer to execute.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE (faster — smaller tiles, less smem pressure)
BLOCK_M : tl.constexpr = 32
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 32
# B-load with tl.trans (bank conflicts but smaller smem footprint)
offs_b_n_col = offs_b_n[:, None]          # [BLOCK_N, 1]
offs_k_row   = offs_k[None, :] + k_idx*BLOCK_K  # [1, BLOCK_K]
b_T = tl.load(B + offs_b_n_col*832 + offs_k_row)  # [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K]
b   = tl.trans(b_T)                       # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
acc += tl.dot(a, b, ...)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (slower — larger tiles, smem-limited occupancy)
BLOCK_M : tl.constexpr = 64
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 64
# Canonical B-load, no tl.trans, but 3x smem footprint
offs_k_b = offs_k[:, None] + k_idx*BLOCK_K  # [BLOCK_K, 1]
offs_n_b = offs_b_n[None, :]                 # [1, BLOCK_N]
b = tl.load(B + offs_k_b*stride_bk + offs_n_b*stride_bn)  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
acc += tl.dot(a, b, ...)
applicable_when: Never: this combined change caused a severe regression. The canonical B-load pattern itself is structurally correct, but pairing it with 2x tile size increases on a kernel already constrained by shared memory limits is counterproductive.
do_not_apply_when: Do not simultaneously enlarge BLOCK_M and BLOCK_K when the kernel is already near the shared-memory-per-block limit (Block Limit Shared Mem ≤ 9). Doubling both tile dimensions quadruples the shared memory footprint, which cuts the smem-limited block count per SM and reduces theoretical occupancy. On this kernel, the bank conflict problem (12-18 way conflicts, ~75-81% MIO stall fraction) persists regardless of the load pattern change — the structural access pattern driving conflicts was not resolved by removing tl.trans. Do not increase BLOCK_K beyond 32 on this kernel without first verifying that smem usage stays within the limit that preserves the original Block Limit Shared Mem value.
framework_notes: In Triton, dynamic shared memory per block scales with BLOCK_M * BLOCK_K * dtype_size for the A tile and BLOCK_K * BLOCK_N * dtype_size for the B tile. Doubling both BLOCK_M and BLOCK_K multiplies smem by 4x for the A tile and 2x for the B tile. The TheoreticalOccupancy rule in NCU will flag when Block Limit Shared Mem drops below Block Limit Registers — this is the signal that smem is the binding occupancy constraint. Registers per thread also increased from 64 to 92, indicating the compiler spilled or allocated more registers for the larger accumulator tile.

strategy_title: Removing Persistent Kernel Loop Regresses Small-Grid GEMMs
strategy_description: Converting a persistent-kernel (while-loop over tiles per SM) to a standard one-tile-per-block kernel while adding @triton.autotune with only num_stages/num_warps variants caused a ~24% regression (0.766x). The persistent kernel's tile-loop amortizes launch overhead and keeps SMs busy across multiple tiles per block; removing it with the same 16-block grid left achieved occupancy completely unchanged at 6.25% while warp cycles per issued instruction worsened from 7.61 to 10.59 and L1/TEX throughput dropped from 87.9% to 68.9%. The 12-way shared memory bank conflict count (~745k excessive wavefronts) was completely unchanged, confirming that adding num_stages alone cannot resolve structural bank conflicts caused by column-major B-matrix strides.
applicable_when: Never: this change caused regression. The persistent kernel pattern is preferable when grid_size << sm_count (here 16 blocks vs 132 SMs), as it keeps SMs busy by processing multiple tiles per block.
do_not_apply_when: Do not remove the persistent kernel tile-loop when grid_size is much smaller than SM count. The persistent loop is the only mechanism keeping SMs active across all tiles; removing it with the same grid size leaves occupancy unchanged while adding scheduling overhead. Adding @triton.autotune with only num_stages/num_warps (no tile size changes) does NOT resolve 12-way shared memory bank conflicts — the SharedMemoryConflicts wavefront count was identical before and after (~745k), confirming num_stages alone cannot fix structural bank conflict patterns caused by column-major memory strides.
framework_notes: In Triton, num_stages controls async software pipeline depth for global→smem copies. It can hide global memory latency but does NOT reorder shared memory access patterns or add padding — it cannot eliminate bank conflicts caused by column-major B-matrix strides (stride_bn=832). The persistent kernel pattern (while tile_id < num_tiles: ... tile_id += NUM_SMS) is a Triton-specific idiom for wave-quantization mitigation on small grids. This regression was reproduced across two separate iterations (iter 3 and iter 4) with consistent metrics, confirming the causal relationship.
